title: What Are You Going to Do With What You Know?
author: Schafer, Kathleen
summary: Executive coach Kathleen Schafer argues that decades of self-discovery tools, strengths assessments, Enneagram, personality typing, have made people good at understanding themselves but not necessarily good at converting that understanding into contribution to others. Revisiting Richard Bolles' What Color Is Your Parachute? and her own Leadership Connection Model, she argues self-awareness becomes leadership only when a person's particular gifts are deliberately offered in service of a team, family, or community, rather than kept as private insight. She contrasts market-assigned measures of value, salary, title, status, with harder-to-price contributions like trust-building or noticing a systemic flaw from the inside. The piece closes with a practical challenge: bring one thing you know about yourself into a meeting or relationship this week and use it in service of someone else.
points: Argues self-development becomes leadership only when insight is turned into contribution to others.
Distinguishes market-assigned value (salary, title, status) from harder-to-price contributions like trust-building or noticing systemic flaws.
Offers a concrete practice: name what you're good at and deliberately offer it in a specific room or relationship this week.
Frames differences among people as functional rather than merely expressive: 'the whole' needs them.
quotes: Because we have gotten very good at asking: Who am I? I am less certain we have become equally good at asking: What am I going to do with what I know?
This, to me, is where self-development becomes leadership. We take what we have discovered and put it into relationship with the world around us.
The person who knows how to create trust. The neighbor who connects people. The employee who sees the flaw in a system because she actually works inside it every day.
Perhaps our uniqueness was never intended to end with self-expression. Perhaps it is meant to become contribution.
Bolles gave people permission to ask different questions: What do I love? What am I good at? What kind of environment brings out the best in me? What do I actually want from my life?
